lessons.title: Making Polite Requests

items.exampleMeaning: Could you help me, please? I am lost.

items.example: Por favor, ¿me puede decir su nombre?
items.exampleMeaning: Please, can you tell me your name?
Could you give me your phone number?

items.example: Me gustaría saber la hora de la reunión.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like to know the time of the meeting.
Would it be possible to change the appointment?

items.example: Aprecio su ayuda con el informe.
items.exampleMeaning: I appreciate your help with the report.

lessons.tip: Use '¿Puede...?' for polite requests. Remember to say 'por favor' to be more polite.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Hello, can you help me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, of course. What do you need?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Could you give me your name?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: My name is Ana. And you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Me gustaría saber su número de teléfono.
dialogue.meaning: I would like to know your phone number.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Claro, es cinco cinco cinco uno dos tres cuatro.
dialogue.meaning: Sure, it is five five five one two three four.

scenario.partnerRole: A is a customer service representative.
scenario.learnerRole: B is a customer seeking assistance.
scenario.brief: You need help with a task. Ask politely for the representative's name and phone number.
scenario.goal: You will politely ask for information.

lessons.title: Spelling Names

items.exampleMeaning: How do you spell your name?
It is spelled A-N-A.
Can you repeat it, please?

items.example: Lo siento, no entendí su nombre.
items.exampleMeaning: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your name.
Can you speak more slowly, please?

items.example: Su nombre es fácil de recordar.
items.exampleMeaning: Your name is easy to remember.

lessons.tip: When asking for spelling, use '¿Cómo se escribe...?' to get clear information.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Hello, how do you spell your name?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: It is spelled J-U-A-N.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Can you repeat it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Sure, it is spelled J-U-A-N.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: I'm sorry, I didn't understand.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: No hay problema. Es fácil de recordar.
dialogue.meaning: No problem. It's easy to remember.

scenario.brief: You need to introduce yourself. Ask how to spell your name and repeat it.
scenario.goal: You will practice spelling your name.

lessons.title: Leaving a Message

items.exampleMeaning: Can I leave a message for Ana?

items.example: Dígale que la reunión es a las tres.
items.exampleMeaning: Tell her that the meeting is at three.

items.example: Lo siento, no está disponible ahora.
items.exampleMeaning: I'm sorry, he/she is not available now.
When can he/she call me back?
Please, call me later.

items.example: Gracias por su mensaje, lo aprecio.
items.exampleMeaning: Thank you for your message, I appreciate it.

lessons.tip: When leaving a message, use '¿Puedo dejar un mensaje?' to ask permission.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Hello, can I leave a message?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, of course. For whom?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Dígale que la reunión es a las tres.
dialogue.meaning: Tell him/her that the meeting is at three.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Lo siento, no está disponible ahora.
dialogue.meaning: I'm sorry, he/she is not available now.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: When can he/she call me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Please, call me later.

scenario.brief: You want to leave a message for someone who is not available. Ask if you can leave a message.
scenario.goal: You will successfully leave a message.

lessons.title: Taking a Message

items.exampleMeaning: What message should I take for Ana?
Who is calling, please?
What is your phone number?
I will write it down in the agenda.

items.example: ¿Cuál es la hora de la reunión?
items.exampleMeaning: What time is the meeting?

items.example: Gracias por la información sobre la reunión.
items.exampleMeaning: Thank you for the information about the meeting.

lessons.tip: When taking a message, ask '¿Qué mensaje debo tomar?' to clarify what to write.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Hello, who is calling?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I am Juan. What message should I take?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Dígale que me llame a las cinco.
dialogue.meaning: Tell him/her to call me at five.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: What is your number?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Es cinco cinco cinco uno dos tres cuatro.
dialogue.meaning: It is five five five one two three four.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Lo anotaré. Gracias por la información.
dialogue.meaning: I will write it down. Thank you for the information.

scenario.brief: You need to take a message for a colleague. Ask who is calling and what message to take.
scenario.goal: You will successfully take a message.
